title: This magnetic accessory brings true flash back to phones
summary: The $85 accessory is iPhone-only for now, but Godox says Android support is coming.
body: TL;DR The $85 Godox A2 brings real xenon flash to smartphones. It’s iPhone-only for now, but the company says Android support is “under development.” Android devices led the way with built-in xenon flash, but abandoned the idea over a decade ago. Many of these camera modes, however, become something you try once or twice and then proceed to forget about . Magic Capture is a Pixel 11 feature that uses Gemini models to analyze roughly 400 video frames and select the best ones to save as photos. As someone who often goes to sporting events and concerts, I thought this feature could’ve been useful enough to keep a Pixel 11 in my pocket year-round. So, I spent weeks testing Magic Capture at the zoo, at a concert, and even at a yo-yo tournament.

title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer
summary: From intrusive ads to clunky software, the smart home landscape has a lot of room to improve. The HomeView could help.
body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . The idea that I could control connected devices with a tap, without having to shout commands at a speaker or pull out my phone, was incredibly appealing. Want to turn off the lights? Just tap a button. Simple, practical. Fast forward to today, and it’s hard not to feel like the category has gone nowhere. Google’s Nest Hub displays are getting long in the tooth, while Amazon’s Echo Show lineup has become increasingly difficult to recommend when so much of the screen real estate is effectively used as a digital billboard.
